messages:
maria: Heads up — we started getting intermittent fnhook payloads where fields flip types across requests (string vs number). Our strict schema path treats that as a hard reject and it’s inflating reject_count and billing alerts.
aj: Can you drop an example log? @hao please take a look.
hao: Example: `{"user_id": 12345, "action": "charge", "attempts": 3}` vs `{"user_id": "12345", "action": "charge", "attempts": "3"}`. Alert link: https://logs.redwood/internal/794321
lex: That’s noisy. Do we currently meter these as rejects (affects quota/billing) or soft-fail them?
maria: Today they flow strict-validate -> REJECT. That increments quota and triggers SLA alerts. Many partners send numeric ids as strings so we see sustained noise.
aj: Proposal: add a ValidationStatus.AMBIGUOUS_TYPE and treat it as a soft-fail by default. Routing will send AMBIGUOUS_TYPE to a degrade/fallback route instead of immediate reject. We still sample payloads for telemetry.
hao: Implementation sketch: validator returns {status: AMBIGUOUS_TYPE, normalized_payload: ..., original_payload_key: s3://...}. Routing layer maps AMBIGUOUS_TYPE -> SOFT_FAIL path with metadata `fallback=true`. Keep original for reprocess.
maria: Telemetry requirements: expose `validation_reason=ambiguous_type`, `validation_sample_rate`, and a redacted example. Default sample_rate=0.01. No raw PII in samples; store only minimal keys.
lex: Console UX asks for a new per-route tile: ambiguous_type rate, trend sparkline, top offending fields, and a redacted example payload button. Also show a small estimation of cost delta between strict reject vs degrade route so owners can decide.
aj: Rollout plan: canary soft-fail for 5% of traffic, flag `fnhook_ambig_softrollout` per-route/account. Default behavior stays strict until canary passes.
hao: Quick config YAML prototype: 
```
validation:
  ambiguous_type:
    handling: soft_fail
    sample_rate: 0.01
    canary_pct: 5
```
maria: Billing Q: should we charge for the original route cost or the final executed route when ambiguous_type triggers fallback? My read: bill actual final execution only, but emit a `validation_impact` metric for finance reconciliation.
lex: Agree on billing the final execution. Keep a separate metric for `validation_incidents` so usage reports can show pattern. Also add an account-level toggle in Console for strict mode enforcement.
aj: SRE concerns: if fallback volumes increase rapidly we need fallback saturation alarms. Tie alerts to dimensions: `route_id` + `fallback=true`. Threshold: sustained >10% fallback => fire ops-bot.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT CONFIG UPDATED: fallback-rate threshold set to 10% for routegroup:fnhooks. Notifications to #eng-oncall.
hao: I’ll open a PR that adds the ambiguous_type enum to the validator, updates routing mapping, and implements sampling export. Will include unit tests for type-coercion heuristic and an end-to-end canary plan.
maria: Please add a dashboard migration: backfill `ambiguous_type` timeseries so older graphs don’t break and include runbook steps for when to flip to strict reject.
lex: Product wants an opt-in immediate strict toggle for customers who prefer strict failures. Add per-account config in Console and an audit log entry when toggled.
aj: 30 min sync tomorrow to review PR + canary steps. Inviting product and billing for charge semantics.
maria: Action items: @hao open PR, @aj drive canary, @lex spec per-account toggle and dashboard tile.
